title: Bass 2004 outer AF biaxial vs uniaxial axial stress at E11 = 0.07 (typical specimen)

quantity.name: axial stress at E11 = 0.07
quantity.definition: axial Lagrangian stress S11 required to reach axial strain E11 = 0.07 with the circumferential strain held at E22 (biaxial) or free (uniaxial)

source.authors: Bass EC, Ashford FA, Segal MR, Lotz JC
source.sample: 5 outer anterior AF cruciform (bone-AF-bone with circumferential AF 'wings') specimens from 5 lumbar motion segments (3 L3-L4, 2 L4-L5) of 5 autopsy spines, Thompson grade I-II

protocol.summary: Outer anterior AF slice with vertebral bone at top/bottom (bone ~10 mm wide) and circumferential AF wings gripped by hooks; thickness 1.57+-0.14 mm; physiologic saline bath; 3 biaxial preconditioning cycles (axial strain with E22 held 0, to 1.0 MPa axial or 1.2 MPa circumferential), 15 min re-equilibration; 0.5 N axial preload; axial deformation at <0.0001 /s with circumferential Lagrangian strain E22 held at 0, +-0.0125, +-0.025, +0.0375 (biaxial) or free (uniaxial); strain from optical grid (~3.3 x 3.0 mm) in the centre; stress = force / undeformed area.
how_to_simulate: Model the cruciform bone-AF-bone specimen (AF thickness ~1.6 mm, bone 10 mm wide; Ghezelbash 2021 used w=20, ww=10, h=12, hw=9 mm) with outer anterior fibre architecture
Uniaxial: pull circumferential wings (or axial bones) with the other direction free; biaxial: pull axially at <0.0001 /s while holding central E22 constant
Report stress vs central Lagrangian strain from a 3x3 mm marker grid

extraction.check_notes: Values quoted in text for the typical specimen of Fig 3. Full biaxial curves (6 E22 levels, Fig 3a,b) overlap heavily and were not digitised. Table 1 strain-energy coefficients are fits (not extracted). doi not printed.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (or inside [min, max] when no SD)
